full_judgment:
2. The case of the plaintiff-respondents No. 1, in brief, is that the plaintiff-company carries on the business as shipping, carrier, agency and chatterer. When the plaintiff company takes agency of any foreign vessel then it takes over all the responsibilities of that Vessel. When the plaintiff company acts as a feeder vessel than goods are carried on from the foreign vessel and released it at the Chittagong port and issues the Bill of lading in the name of the original carrier vessel. Respondent Nos. 2-4 carry on their-business in Singapore and have their branch office in Bangladesh. The plaintiff company possesses several vessels namely M. V. Bangla Biraj Banga Vanik. M.V. Banga Lanka. M.V. Banga Birol. M.V. Banga Bijoy and three more charter vessels. Respondent Nos. 2-4 used to get the imported goods discharged at the Singapore port, which were imported by the container-carrying vessel. And the plaintiff company carried the container in their own vessel through transshipment from the mother vessel in Singapore and got the same discharged in the Chittagong port. The plaintiff company was the local agent of the transshipment and had all the responsibilities in this regard and also performed the function of the cargo forwarding and others. Defendant No. 3 looked after the business of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in Bangladesh before. The plaintiff company the M/s. Intrance Ltd. was the agent of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 M/s. Intrance Ltd. used to store the empty containers in the private bonded warehouse of the proforma defendant No. 5 and defendant No. 2 was the-owner of those containers. The plaintiff company had no written agreement with the proforma defendant No. 5-petitioner Shafi Motors. But the plaintiff company had an agency agreement with the defendant No. 3. The plaintiff company issued the declaration under section 55 of the Customs Act whereby it took over all the liabilities of the defendant No. 3 and the customs accepted the same US$ 22850 for carrying the goods in Chittagong-Singapore line by their own vessels of the plaintiff company was due to the defendants. The plaintiff company is liable to pay the dues of the Chittagong Customs Department against the defendants under the joint declaration. Furthermore, to make good the damages for delayed discharge of goods, over duty charge of the customs and the goods falls short or damaged, the plaintiff company is liable for making payment of the decreed amount of suit. The proforma defendant No. 5 petitioner. M/s. Shafi Motors claimed Tk. 34,62,240/- for keeping the containers in its ICD upto 30th September 2001. But the plaintiff company could not pay the dues of the proforma defendant-petitioner as it did not get the remittance. In the ICD of the proforma defendant No. 5 petitioner, there is 863 containers. The plaintiff company forwarded the bills of its dues and other dues as the agent of the defendants on line out the defendants remained silent. Thereafter the plaintiff company issued several requests written and verbal, but the defendants remained silent and subjected the plaintiff company to suffer huge losses. Therefore finding no other alternative remedies, the plaintiff company instituted the instant suit for recovery of money. The defendant's only property in Bangladesh are the empty containers in the ICD of Dhaka and Chittagong. The plaintiff company has come to know from a reliable source that the defendant is trying to change its business and by removing the empty containers trying to misappropriate the money of the plaintiff-respondent No. 1. Now if the defendants succeeds in doing the above the decree would be infructuous and the plaintiff company shall be subjected to face irreparable loss of money. Therefore, the plaintiff company prayed for a money decree with a petition for attachment before judgment of the empty containers within the jurisdiction of the Court. 

 4. After hearing the parties the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Chittagong decreed the suit. 

 8. It is on record that a copy of the application dated 2.9.2003 with endorsement was filed along with the petition in Court stating that the petitioner was not available for service of the same and that the order of stay was vacated by the High Court Division subject to furnishing bank guarantee for Tk. 87,25,622.80 as security for decree of the petitioner on the understanding that after security furnished the petitioner would have no objection to the execution of the decree. In the course of execution, the Executing court was of the view that inspecting the conditions of the containers in question was a step necessary for sale of them. It appears that on an application at the instance of the plaintiff-decree-holder for appointment of an experienced surveyor having the knowledge of handling the containers, the same was allowed asking the decree-holder to deposit Tk. 5000/- immediately. The High Court Division on consideration of the application of the petitioner observed that it did not show at all why the petitioner is likely to be affected by any such order of the Court in appointing a surveyor for inspection of the condition of the containers in question and found that no in-justice would be caused to the petitioner due to the impugned order.
